title: Hermetic GeGLU Airlocks and Domain-Adaptive Context Distillation: Exact Zero-Crosstalk Multi-Domain Function Embedding in Quantized GGUF Foundation Models
domain: modular capability embedding in quantized LLMs (RISC-V ALU simulation, ARC-AGI grid puzzles, Japanese prose editing)
tasks_benchmarks: 36 self-made held-out tasks (8 RISC-V, 8 ARC-style grid, 8 Japanese prose, 12 general control)

headline_result.text: Appending 512 gated MLP neurons per layer in three layers of a Gemma-4-E4B GGUF and training them by context distillation raised accuracy on 36 self-made held-out tasks from 58.33% (21/36) to 72.22% +/- 2.78% across two runs, with zero log-prob drift on 10 control prompts.

key_claims.claim: Linear orthogonal 'cartridge' edits leaked into unrelated prompts and lowered 42-task accuracy from 69.05% to 64.29%.
key_claims.quote: enabling all 14 orthogonal cartridges simultaneously degraded overall 42-task accuracy from 69.05% (29/42) to 64.29% (27/42).

key_claims.claim: The new neurons are trained by gradient descent (context distillation with AdamW for two epochs), not written by an LLM editor.
key_claims.quote: optimization is restricted to 2 epochs (378 total steps across 189 verified trajectories

key_claims.claim: Mounting airlocks on contiguous layers degraded accuracy to 44.44%.
key_claims.quote: mounting airlocks on four consecutive layers (38 → 39 → 40 → 41) caused positive GeGLU activations to compound across adjacent residual steps during multi-hundred-token autoregressive rollouts, degrading accuracy to 44.44%.

key_claims.claim: Control accuracy was unchanged at 11/12 while the three embedded domains improved by one to four tasks out of eight each.
key_claims.quote: simultaneously boosts RISC-V ALU simulation ( 50.00% -> 62.50% ), ARC-AGI 2D grid reasoning ( 50.00% -> 75.00%–100.00% ), and kousei-jp Japanese prose editing ( 25.00% -> 37.50%

limitations_stated.text: Fewer than 100 training samples per domain cannot produce out-of-family generalisation.
limitations_stated.quote: N < 100 samples cannot induce zero-shot synthesis of entirely untrained instruction extensions

limitations_stated.text: Long control completions are not bit-identical to the base model in many cases, because one gate leaks.
limitations_stated.quote: bit-for-bit string identity across 300-token Control completions is 8/12 in Run A and 4/12 in Run B.

notes_for_review: Despite using 'weight-space programming' as a keyword, this is gradient-trained capability insertion (appended gated neurons plus context distillation with straight-through quantization), with no LLM reading or writing weights, so it falls outside LLM-driven WSP. Evidence is weak: 8 tasks per domain on a self-built suite, two runs, the headline mixes a peak and a mean, and the text is heavy with self-coined terms ('impossibility theorem', 'airlock', 'axiom'). Single pseudonymous author, no peer review, and it does not cite the MIT work.
